title: What Does the Bible Say About Meditation? 29 Verses
description: What the Bible says about meditation: meditating on God's word day and night, the psalms, being still and how it differs from emptying the mind.
keywords: what does the bible say about meditation
meditate on his word day and night
summary: Forms of meditate appear in 22 verses of the World English Bible, and almost all of them mean thinking over and murmuring God's words, not emptying the mind. The Lord tells Joshua to meditate on the book of the law day and night (Joshua 1:8), and Psalm 1:2 says the blessed person delights in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night. Psalm 119 is the longest meditation, with the writer meditating on God's precepts, statutes and promises (verses 15, 23, 48, 97, 148). Isaac meditates in the field at evening (Genesis 24:63), David meditates on God in the night watches (Psalm 63:6), and Paul tells Timothy to meditate on these things (1 Timothy 4:15). The verses below follow those threads.

faqs.a: Yes, when it means reflecting on God, his word and his works (Joshua 1:8, Psalm 1:2, Psalm 77:12). The Hebrew word hagah suggests murmuring or musing aloud over a text, closer to slow reading than to clearing the mind.

faqs.q: How is Christian meditation different from other kinds?
faqs.a: The Bible's pattern fills the mind with God's word and character (Philippians 4:8, Colossians 3:2); many Eastern practices aim to empty it. Psalm 46:10, 'Be still, and know that I am God', is about trusting God, not about a technique.

faqs.q: How do you meditate on Scripture?
faqs.a: Choose a short passage, read it slowly several times, ask what it says about God, and pray it back (Psalm 119:15, 119:97). Psalm 1:2-3 says the one who meditates is like a tree planted by streams of water.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about being still?
faqs.a: Psalm 46:10 says to be still and know that God is God, Psalm 4:4 says to commune with your heart on your bed and be still, and Psalm 62:5 says to wait in silence for God alone.
